steps.body: Shapes we can **hold**! A ball is a **sphere**. A dice is a **cube**. A can is a **cylinder**. A hat is a **cone**.

hotspots.label: cone

hotspots.label: cylinder

steps.body: Name a solid in a new position.
explanationVariants: It has one pointy end and a round bottom — that is a cone.
A cone keeps its point and its round bottom, even lying on its side.

widget.prompt: An ice-cream shape lies on its side. It has a point at one end and a round bottom. Which solid is it?

options.label: A cylinder
options.feedback: A cylinder has two flat round ends and no point.

options.label: A cube
options.feedback: A cube is boxy with flat square faces, not a point.

options.label: A cone
options.feedback: Yes — a cone keeps its point and round bottom even on its side.

options.label: A sphere
options.feedback: A sphere is round all over and has no point.

hints: Turn the shape in your mind. Does it have a point?
It has one pointy end, so it is not round all over — that rules out a ball.
A round bottom and one point make a cone.

steps.body: Solid, or just a flat picture?
explanationVariants: A ball, a die, a can, and a party hat are solids you could actually hold. A picture or cutout of a circle or square is flat — it has no solid shape at all.
Solid names like sphere and cube are for things with real depth, like a ball or a box. A flat circle or square drawn on paper is not a solid, even though it can look round or boxy.

widget.prompt: Some of these are real solids you could hold. A couple are only FLAT pictures. Sort each one into its group.

items.label: a basketball
items.feedback: A basketball is round every way you turn it — a solid sphere, not just a flat circle.

items.label: an orange
items.feedback: An orange is round all over, just like a ball — a solid sphere.

items.label: a die, like from a board game
items.feedback: A die is boxy with flat square faces all around — a solid cube.

items.label: a paper towel roll
items.feedback: A paper towel roll has round flat ends and stands like a can — a solid cylinder.

items.label: a birthday hat
items.feedback: A birthday hat is round at the bottom and comes to one point — a solid cone.

items.label: a circle cut flat out of paper
items.feedback: A paper cutout is flat and thin, like a page — it is not a solid you could stack or hold like a ball.

items.label: a square drawn flat on a whiteboard
items.feedback: A drawing on a board is flat, not a solid you could hold — a real cube has 6 flat faces you can feel.

widget.missFeedback: Ask first: could you actually pick this up and hold it, or is it just a flat picture?
widget.successFeedback: Yes — round-all-over things are spheres, boxy things are cubes, can-shaped things are cylinders, pointy-round things are cones, and flat pictures are not solids at all.

hints: First ask if the thing has real depth you could hold, or if it is just a flat picture.
A flat circle or square drawn on paper is NOT a solid, even though it looks round or boxy.
Round all over is a sphere, boxy is a cube, can-shaped is a cylinder, and pointy-round is a cone.
